text:
Garry Kasparov was born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, and adopted the surname Kasparov at age twelve. He began serious chess study at age seven, training at Mikhail Botvinnik's chess school. He quickly rose through the ranks, winning the World Junior Chess Championship in 1980 and becoming a Grandmaster the same year. He became the No. 1 ranked player in the world in January 1984, holding the record for 12 years, and won the World Chess Championship in 1985.
Kasparov's career involved numerous intense matches against his rival, Karpov. In 1986, he successfully defended his title. Following his break with FIDE in 1993, he won the PCA title against Nigel Short. After losing the title to Kramnik in 2000, he continued to compete, although he announced his retirement from regular competitive chess in March 2005. Post-retirement, he engaged in activities like coaching Carlsen and training Hikaru Nakamura, and he has been politically active, becoming a vocal critic of the Putin administration.
